glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.T-cell-mediated: Driven by T lymphocytes rather than antibodies.
glossary.Type 1 diabetes: Diabetes from autoimmune destruction of the pancreatic beta cells.
glossary.Autoimmune thyroid disease: Thyroid disorders caused by autoantibodies, such as Graves' disease and Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
glossary.Non-bloody diarrhoea: Loose stools without blood, pointing away from colitis.
glossary.Extensor surfaces: The outer sides of limbs over the extending joints, such as elbows and knees.
glossary.Cutaneous manifestation: A sign of a disease seen in the skin.
glossary.Adherence: How well a patient sticks to treatment, here the gluten-free diet.
glossary.Bone mineral density: How much mineral is packed into bone; low density means fragile bones.
glossary.Duodenal biopsy: A small tissue sample taken from the duodenum during endoscopy.
glossary.Jejunal: Relating to the jejunum, the middle part of the small bowel.
glossary.Gastroscopy: A camera passed through the mouth to view the oesophagus, stomach and duodenum.
glossary.Total IgA: Overall IgA level, checked to make sure IgA-based tests are not falsely negative.
glossary.Anti-TTG IgG: IgG antibody against tissue transglutaminase, used when the patient is IgA deficient.
glossary.Macrocytic anaemia: Anaemia with large red cells, often from B12 or folate deficiency.
glossary.Mixed deficiency: Lack of more than one nutrient at once, e.g. iron plus B12, which can leave MCV normal.
glossary.Blood film: A smear of blood looked at under the microscope.
glossary.Leprosy: A chronic Mycobacterium leprae infection of skin and nerves.
glossary.Toxoplasmosis: Infection with the parasite Toxoplasma gondii.
glossary.PCP: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, a fungal pneumonia in the immunosuppressed.
glossary.Folic acid: Vitamin B9 supplement that reduces neural tube defects in pregnancy.
glossary.Surveillance: Regular checks to catch complications early.
glossary.Immunogenicity: How strongly something provokes an immune response.
glossary.Inflammatory cascade: A chain of immune signals that amplifies inflammation.
glossary.Genetically susceptible: Carrying genes that raise the risk of a disease.
glossary.Absorptive surface area: The total area of gut lining available to absorb nutrients, made huge by villi.
glossary.Fat-soluble vitamins: Vitamins A, D, E and K, absorbed with fat.
glossary.Immune complex: Antibody bound to its antigen; can deposit in tissues and cause inflammation.
glossary.Dermis: The layer of skin beneath the epidermis.
glossary.Malignant transformation: Normal cells changing into cancer cells.
glossary.Villi: Finger-like projections of the small bowel lining that absorb nutrients.
